q: The constrained coding capacity theorem (Marcus–Siegel, Adler–Coppersmith–Hassner) says a binary source at rate R can be encoded into constrained channel X (subshift with entropy h_top(X)) iff:
opts: R ≤ h_top(X) and h_top(X) is a rational multiple of log 2
exp: Rate R bits/symbol can be encoded into X at rate R/h_top(X) output symbols per input symbol if R < h_top(X). The existence of finite-state encoders with sliding-window decoders additionally requires h_top(X)/log 2 to be rational (so rate ratios are rational).
